# 4 December 1984

The administrative wing is dark when she arrives. Seven in the morning, the overhead strip not yet on, the corridor windows still the gray before proper daylight. She can hear the overnight caretaker somewhere at the far end, the sound of the cart's metal wheel against the linoleum. She does not call out to him. She goes directly to Mița's desk and lines the payroll envelopes along the front edge — one per name, alphabetical, sealed and initialed the night before. She counts them as she sets them down. Fourteen. The same as every month.

She does not sign the distribution sheet.

She goes to her own desk. She does not hang her coat. She sets her bag on the floor beside the chair and does not open it. She sits for a moment with her hands flat on the desk and then she opens the bottom shelf of the bookcase and lifts out the 1983 ledger — black cover, her own label starting to lift at the lower right corner, the binding soft from two years on the shelf.

She has produced this ledger on demand three times: the spring audit, the year-end reconciliation, the mill director's signature on the October figures. Each time she has set it on the desk and opened it to the requested page and said nothing while whoever was reading it finished. Each time she has put it back on the shelf afterward and the paper in the spine was still there.

She holds the ledger spine-down over her desk and waits. The paper slides free — a moment of resistance, a small sound, and then it is in her palm. A single sheet, folded in thirds, the creases gone soft from fourteen months in one position.

She sets the ledger back on the shelf, spine straight with the others.

She does not unfold the paper. She folds it once more, the same fold, the same direction, along the same crease, and puts it into her left breast pocket.

She stands. She buttons her coat.

Right coat pocket: N4, where it has been since the second of December.
Left breast pocket: N1, where it has been since October 1983.

She puts on her gloves. She picks up the pen from her desk and sets it parallel to the edge — the way it sits when she has not been in. She turns off the lamp.

She goes out through the side door onto the service road.

---

The cold outside is complete and still — not the cold with wind, but the cold that does not need it. A thin layer of snow from the night before, already dirty along the road edges, pressed hard underfoot and squeaking at every step. The sky is pale yellow to the east, the sun at the rooflines but not above them yet.

She goes around the outer fence to the main avenue and turns toward the market. Strada 22 Decembrie is fifteen minutes at her pace. She does not change her pace.

At the corner of the market, the bread queue is six deep. Ilinca walks by the end of it and does not look at anyone in it.

She passes the post office — the notice board outside with the water-stain across the lower right corner that has been there since September. She passes the pharmacy, grille still down, the window dark. She passes the bloc where Georgeta lives. Third floor, second window from the right — the curtains closed, the light behind them not on. She passes the bloc where Livia Moldovan lives. She does not look up at either of them.

She turns onto Strada 22 Decembrie.

The station is visible from the corner. Stone facade, two stories, the national emblem above the public entrance, an official vehicle parked in the yard to the side. She pushes the door open.

---

Inside: warm air and the smell of floor wax and something underneath it, the particular smell of rooms where forms accumulate over years. A long counter with a frosted glass partition, two stations, only one occupied. The duty officer is young — round-faced, the collar of his uniform one size large for his neck. He looks up from what he is writing.

She says: I need to speak with Lieutenant Munteanu. Regarding the Petrescu matter.

He says: Your name.

She says: Roșca, Ilinca. Mill administration.

He writes this down. He says: Wait there.

There is a bench to her left. Two men are sitting on it, not speaking to each other, both in their fifties, both with the look of people who have been waiting longer than they expected. She stays at the counter. She sets her gloved hands on the counter edge and then takes them off and holds them at her sides.

From behind the partition she can hear a typewriter — three quick strokes, a pause, three more — and then a door somewhere opening. And then a door closing. And then nothing, except the two men on the bench and her own breathing and the sound of a vehicle in the yard outside starting its engine and then going quiet again.

The duty officer comes back through the door at the partition's end. He says: Come through.

---

The corridor beyond is narrower than she expected. Linoleum floor in a color between green and gray, scuffed to nothing along the center. Doors on both sides, most closed. At the far end a window looks out on the courtyard — she can see the official vehicle and the frost still white on the upper course of brickwork on the wall opposite. They go up one short flight of stairs, uncarpeted, and along another corridor. The duty officer stops at the second door on the right. It is open.

---

Munteanu is at his desk. The Petrescu dosar is open in front of him, its cover folded back, and she can see the working pages — forms, notebook sheets, printed headings filled in by hand. Along the left edge of the desk: seven evidence envelopes in a row. She counts them. Seven. She knows the dates they arrived. She knows what each one holds. To the right of the envelopes: his notebook, open to a page of handwriting dense enough that the white of the page is almost gone. At the far corner of the desk, a coffee cup with the coffee dried to a ring at the bottom.

He looks up from the dosar. He looks at her. There is a moment before he says anything. He does not look surprised. He looks at her the way a man looks at a figure that finally matches the column it belongs in.

He says: Tovarășă Roșca?

She says: Yes.

He says: Please, sit down.

The chair across from the desk is wooden and straight-backed, a worn patch on the seat. She sits.

She takes N1 from her left breast pocket, unfolding it as she lifts it free. She takes N4 from her right coat pocket. She sets both documents on the desk in front of him — flat, side by side, N1 to the left, N4 to the right — and removes her hands from both pages.

He looks at them. He does not pick either one up immediately. He reads a few words of each from where he is sitting. Then he picks up N1.

---

1. Keep her warm and lying down. Someone stays with her the whole night.
2. Small sips of water, often. Nothing else by mouth for six hours.
3. Count the cloths. Write the number and the hour on the paper by the bed.
4. If she sleeps, wake her every hour and speak to her until she answers you properly.
5. No visitors. No telephone. If anyone asks, she has the influenza.
6. Burn nothing until she is well. Wash and keep.
7. Two cloths in one hour is too many.
8. A fever that will not come down by morning is too long.
   [ 7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why.
     Do not wait for the morning. ]

He reads it line by line. She watches his eyes track down the page. When he reaches line eight he slows. His eyes go to the bracket below it — the indented lines, the closing bracket — and he reads to the end and holds the page.

He sets N1 down. He picks up N4.

---

1. Keep her warm and lying down. Someone stays with her the whole night.
2. Small sips of water, often. Nothing else by mouth for six hours.
3. Count the cloths. Write the number and the hour on the paper by the bed.
4. If she sleeps, wake her every hour and speak to her until she answers you properly.
5. No visitors. No telephone. If anyone asks, she has the influenza.
6. Burn nothing until she is well. Wash and keep.
7. Two cloths in one hour is too many.
8. A fever that will not come down by morning is too long.
9. 7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning.

He reads it and then reads it again from line seven. He sets N4 beside N1 and looks at both pages at the same time. His eyes move from one to the other. He looks at the lower half of the left-hand page — the bracket, the indented lines. He looks at the lower half of the right-hand page — the numbered ninth line, flush with the margin.

She does not speak.

He says: Did you make these?

She says: Yes.

He says: Which one first?

She says: The one with the bracket.

He looks at the two documents once more. Then he reaches for the telephone.

He dials the internal line. It rings twice.

He says: This is Munteanu. I need you to release Marcu Doina from the holding section. She can sign for her things and go.

A pause. She can hear the voice at the other end, small and metallic.

He says: Immediately.

He puts the telephone down.

He picks it up again. He dials a different number. A longer wait this time.

He says: Captain. This is Munteanu. The Petrescu matter — I've resolved it. I have the originating party here in my office. He says her name. Her employer. A pause, the captain's voice rising once. He says: A voluntary approach. This morning. Yes. I can have the full documentation to you by end of business. He listens. He says: Understood.

He puts the telephone down.

---

Somewhere along the corridor a door opens and then closes.

He pulls the right-hand drawer open and takes out a blank form — white, the Miliția heading printed across the top — and sets it on the desk beside the evidence envelopes. He picks up his pen.

He writes her name first, last name before first. Then the date. Then her address.

He writes on.

The two documents are still between them on the desk. N1 to the left, N4 to the right. She can read both from where she is sitting. She has read both so many times that the lines run in sequence whether she means them to or not — eight lines and a bracket on the left; nine lines on the right; the same words in both, and the ninth line in a different place, and everything that came from that. She has not moved. Her coat is still buttoned. Her hands are in her lap.

He writes on.

The writing on both documents is hers.

She sits.

# Reader Act 1 Assessment — Chapters 01–10

## What's working

**Voice discipline.** The three registers are fully realized and distinguishable from the first sentence of each chapter, without exception. Ilinca's close third present lands in procedural tallies: "She is on the last two lines of the October column when the knock comes" (ch 09) is a thought and a fact and a clock simultaneously — the exemplar in the brief could have been lifted from any of her five chapters. Munteanu's third past is careful, orderly, and literary in a way that feels like the state speaking in its native register, which is exactly the brief's intention: "It was the kind of finding that would not survive being described to his captain in its present form, and he understood, with a flatness that surprised him, that he was going to pursue it anyway" (ch 04) is a near-perfect realization of the character brief. Doina is the revelation. "The bridge over the Someș was always the worst part, and I say that as someone who spent two years crossing it in the dark at four-thirty in the morning, which gives me more authority on the subject than I would have liked" (ch 10) is not the wry-and-restrained funny of previous books in this pipeline; it is genuinely nineteen. "I had done the arithmetic once and been depressed by it and had not done it again" (ch 10). The geometry of her "thinking about the word *fairly*, and how it was not the same word as *certainly*, and how it was the only word I had" (ch 06) renders fear through verbal precision without naming it. Doina's voice is the first real comic register this library has produced.

**Fear rendered as procedure.** Ten chapters, not one named fear. The cold comes through the soles of Ilinca's shoes. The woman at the counter folds the dish towel in half and then in half again "until she had a square she had nowhere particular to put" (ch 08). Doina runs cold water on her wrists because "it does something to my heart rate that is worth doing in certain situations" (ch 02). The standard holds without exception through Act I.

**The dramatic irony is in place by chapter 9.** The reader watches Ilinca read N1's bracket — "*take her in. Do not wait for the morning*" — and then construct the mutant line 9 — "*If 7 or 8, take her in in the morning*" — and understands the fatal difference before Ilinca does, and before Ilinca understands it is her cellar copy that is the ancestor. The mechanism works. The irony has fuel to run on through Act II.

**The compounding mechanism is legible.** Ilinca's count advances: 2 (ch 03), 4 (ch 07), 5 (ch 09). Munteanu's copy count advances: 2 (ch 04), 3 (ch 08). The day count is clear from the dated chapter headers. Each chapter forecloses something new: the N2 branch is closed and clean (ch 07); the mutation is confirmed present before Lucia Gal (ch 08); the investigation is visible inside the mill (ch 07) and has reached the production floor (ch 10). No chapter re-measures an already-established count without new pressure.

**The documents as objects.** The grey mill-form paper with blue pencil and a foreman's signature box on the front (ch 08) is a physically distinct thing before it is data. The geography book on the shelf above the coat hooks, between pages 34 and 35 of the watershed drainage diagram, is exactly the right kind of hidden-in-plain-sight. The 1983 ledger with its brown reinforcing tape applied in February when the binding cracked (ch 01) is a state document Ilinca would produce without hesitation — which is precisely what makes it the right hiding place.

**Munteanu's frame.** He is neither villain nor sympathiser, exactly as briefed. The difference between *by the bed* and *beside the bed* as a signal of inherited variation, not copying error (ch 04), is sound police work rendered on the page. He sees the two branches; he sees the mutation is upstream. He is right, and solving the wrong problem, and the chapter never says so.

---

## What's not working

**The canonical N1 text is truncated in chapter 09.** When Ilinca reads the master at her desk, the bracket is rendered as:

> `[ 7 or 8 — take her in. Do not wait for the morning. ]`

The registered canonical text of N1 (record `master-n1`) reads:

> `[ 7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning. ]`

The sentence "Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why." is absent. Chapter 09 is one of the four permitted full printings of N1, so the omission is not a fragment-quotation choice — it is a drift against the canonical record. The loss is functional, not merely formal: "what to say when you get there" is part of the document's practical purpose, and its omission makes the bracket read more clinical than it should. The contrast with the mutant line 9 still lands, but the master is incomplete. This is also inconsistent with chapter 06, where Doina correctly recites the full bracket text from N14 (which matches the canonical form): "*7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning.*" The error is small but confirmable against the record.

**Chapter 07 slightly re-confirms what chapter 03 established.** In chapter 03, Georgeta tells Ilinca that Livia "has kept it to herself." In chapter 07, via Georgeta's daughter: "She says Livia is fine. Quiet. She's been at home, not seeing people... No, she kept it to herself." The new information in chapter 07 is meaningful — Miliția has not yet reached Livia, which is a genuine foreclosure — but the repetition of the core confirmation (Livia kept it, Livia has not passed it on) is slightly redundant. The chapter earns its place through the materials-discrepancy cover and the escalating pressure context, so this falls below the threshold of a structural failure. It's a soft re-measurement: not an orbiting chapter, but a chapter where a beat runs a little long before arriving at the new thing.

---

## Voice slips

**Chapter 09, Ilinca's analysis of the mutation.** After reading the bracket against the mutant line 9, Ilinca explains: "The woman who made that copy was being tidy. She saw nine pieces of information and she numbered them one through nine, because that is what a careful copyist does with nine pieces of information and a numbered list on the page in front of her." This is true, precise, and in Ilinca's idiom — but it is also close to the brief's explicit prohibition on thesis-stating. The brief says the argument must be "carried entirely by the tree of copies — never stated by a character." Ilinca is stating the mechanism of the mutation, which is on the edge of the book's constraint. What saves it is that she is *wrong* — she concludes the mutation entered downstream of all three copies she made, not in N4. The articulation is in the service of a false confidence, not the book's argument. It stays on the right side of the line, but it runs very close to it. A later chapter where a character correctly names the mechanism would cross.

**Chapter 02, Doina, a single phrase.** "I am not asking you to believe it changed anything. I am asking you to believe it is true." This is Doina talking to the reader, which is consistent with her first-person retrospective register — she is giving testimony. But "I am not asking you to believe it changed anything" carries a slight editorial weight, as though Doina is pre-empting the reader's moral judgment. It's one sentence and does not recur, so it does not rise to a finding, but it's the closest the book comes in Act I to a character managing the reader's response rather than reporting to them.

---

## Thread development in Act I

All five threads enter cleanly. Thread 1 (Ilinca's guilty knowledge) runs from false confidence through confirmation of the clean branches to the establishment of the irony gap — Ilinca concludes the error is downstream while the reader knows it is in N4. Thread 2 (Doina's silence) is well-seeded: the woman on the bus is established as unnamed and already past; the silence is passive habit before it becomes active choice; the physical threat becomes visible in chapter 06. Thread 3 (the administrative deadline) enters in chapter 04 with the 31-day clock, is felt in Munteanu's case-building pressure, and will tighten in Act II. Thread 4 (Munteanu's wrong frame) is perfectly established: he solves the genealogy problem with genuine competence and never holds the proposition that the ninth line is a warning, not a step. Thread 5 (the form of the knowledge) opens on the gap between possession and knowing in chapter 02 and is already moving toward internalization in chapter 06 when Doina finds she remembers more than she thought she did.

---

## Pacing

Act I moves quickly and earns its pace. The brief's floor of 1,900 words is met in all ten chapters; no chapter is padding. The physical texture — the November Someș valley, the cold in the administrative wing before six, the loom noise that makes conversation "not possible in any practical sense" — does double duty as atmosphere and clock. The A-B-A-C rotation gives the book a driving rhythm: Ilinca building her private map, then Doina's counterpoint, then Ilinca again, then Munteanu advancing from the other direction. By chapter 10, both collations are moving, the irony is established, and the investigation is inside the mill. Act I delivers its structural contract.

---

## Brief-adherence summary (Act I checks)

1. **POV identifiable in first sentence**: ✓ All ten chapters.  
2. **Both ladders advance**: ✓ Ilinca's count and Munteanu's count both move; day count is clear from dates.  
3. **Day count legible**: ✓ Dated headers, Nov 4–13 across Act I.  
4. **Act I close irony established**: ✓ Ch 09 delivers the contrast between N1's bracket and the mutant line 9.  
5. **Fear as procedure, not named**: ✓ No named fear in any of the ten chapters.  
6. **Doina's voice genuinely funny**: ✓ Her three chapters have consistent comic specificity.  
7. **No thesis stated by any character**: ✓ Borderline in ch 09 but Ilinca is wrong; the mechanism is rendered inside a false conclusion.  
8. **No character explains the tree**: ✓  
9. **Document text against registered records**: **ONE FAILURE.** Ch 09 renders N1 with the bracket truncated — missing "Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why."  
10. **Safety constraint**: ✓ No method, substance, dose, or procedure.

# Reader — Act 2 Assessment (Chapters 11–20)

## Brief-adherence checks for this act

1. **POV legibility at first sentence?** Yes, without exception. Ilinca's chapters open in present-tense procedural close-third ("She does the variance three times"); Doina's open in first-person-past direct address ("The district heating had come on for half an hour in the night"); Munteanu's open in deliberate past close-third with investigative texture ("The two copies occupied the right side of his desk"). The three registers are distinguishable before the second sentence in every chapter.

2. **Both node-count ladders visible?** Yes. Ilinca's count advances in each of her chapters: 5→6 (ch. 11), 6→7 (ch. 13), 7→8 (ch. 15), 8→9 (ch. 17). Munteanu's count advances: 2→3 (ch. 12), 3→4+ (ch. 16, including the canvassed bracket copy), 4→6 (ch. 20). A reader can state both counts at any point in the act without being told them explicitly.

3. **Day count legible?** Yes. The individual chapter dates carry the clock, and key markers are embedded: "Day 12" surfaces in ch. 15 via the canteen conversation; "15 days" is stated explicitly in ch. 16 when the captain calls; "November 24-25, 10 days remain" closes ch. 20.

4. **Act I irony properly established?** Confirmed from Act I groundwork: the reader holds `ninth-line-is-a-warning-not-a-step` entering this act, and the irony is live and visible throughout — most sharply in ch. 16 and ch. 20, where Munteanu reads both versions of line 9 side by side and records the difference as a formatting variable. He has the murder weapon in his notes and does not understand what it is. The gap is functioning.

5. **Safety constraint?** Holding without exception. Every quoted fragment is aftercare only. No chapter acquires method, substance, dose, or procedure at any node.

6. **Fear named?** Near-clean. No instance of "she was afraid" or equivalent. Ch. 14 offers the act's best handling of this constraint: "Eight has the word *morning* in it. Since the beginning of November everything with *morning* in it has acquired a quality I do not have a name for." The refusal to name the feeling is itself in voice. One possible near-miss: ch. 15's final line ("she cannot tell — in the account she keeps, in the column she has been maintaining for thirteen months without a single entry she could not defend — whether what she holds under N4 is a bracket or a nine") names an epistemic gap, not an emotion, and is clean.

---

## What is working

**Voice discipline.** This is the act's primary achievement and it holds across all ten chapters without detectable drift. Ilinca's chapters run entirely in columns and reconciliations; her interiority is expressed as tallies, entries, nodes counted (ch. 13: "Five, and now this: six"; ch. 19: "Munteanu: three. The two counts have been moving in the same direction all month"). Doina's chapters are digressive, honest, retrospectively self-aware in exactly the nineteen-year-old register the brief specified. Munteanu's chapters are deliberate and orderly in the pipeline's default literary voice. The irony that the state's investigator speaks in the most artful register is never pointed out and never needs to be.

**The arrest scene (ch. 18)** is the act's best chapter and one of the book's likely centerpieces. Doina's account of going to the door without looking back, the geography book staying in its locker, the sentence "every sentence of it was true, in the way that a set of true sentences can describe a true thing and leave the whole of the true thing sitting in the middle of them, in the space the sentences make around it, untouched" — this is the exact register the brief demanded: nineteen, honest, retroactively clear-eyed, and not self-exculpating. The pacing of the interrogation scene (measured waiting, specific lies that are technically truths) is controlled throughout.

**The lamp-tilt scene (ch. 17).** Ilinca takes N1 from the ledger, looks at the bracket in forty watts, then tilts the paper until the lower horizontal stroke goes into shadow — physically re-creating the cellar conditions in her kitchen. This is the book's central question rendered as a physical act of testing, not as emotion. It advances the thread (suspicion to near-certainty) without naming the reckoning. It's exactly how this character's mind works.

**Thread development is clean.** Thread 1 moves from false confidence to working suspicion to near-knowledge on schedule. Thread 2's silence is formally enacted in ch. 18, with the crucial moment that Doina does not look back at anything in the room — a physical enactment of the decision before it becomes a decision. Thread 3's deadline goes from implicit to explicit in ch. 16 (captain's call). Thread 4's wrong frame is preserved exactly: Munteanu sees the bracket/numbered distinction in ch. 16 and ch. 20, records it as a formatting variable, asks "which format is the source" (the genealogical question), never asks what the ninth position means for the woman following it. Thread 5 completes the knowledge-to-memory transfer in ch. 14.

**The compounding mechanism has no dead chapters.** Each chapter closes one option: a branch is confirmed clean, a node is now known to the militia, a woman is in state custody, an address is written in a notebook that will not lose it.

---

## What is not working

**Desk-layout scene repetition (chs. 12, 16, 20).** All three Munteanu chapters in this act involve him laying copies across his desk, weighting corners with what is at hand, reading each copy in turn, and making a two-tier note (working notebook vs. formal file). The choreography is identical across all three. The brief's own exemplar passage describes exactly this scene ("He laid the four sheets side by side on the desk and weighted the corners with whatever was nearest"), and ch. 16 reproduces that framing nearly verbatim. Each instance advances something new — ch. 12 establishes the line-9 divergence, ch. 16 reveals the two-branch structure, ch. 20 distinguishes the three-way categorization. But the procedural container is the same each time, and by ch. 20 the reader has learned to expect it. The scene has become a template rather than a discovery. A single desk-layout scene, or at most two, would carry more weight than three.

**Literary-fade ending dominance.** Of the ten chapters, at least five to six end in atmospheric quiet: lamp going off, fog sitting on the street, heat coming on briefly, eyes closed at the kitchen table. The brief explicitly licenses "quiet endings where the chapter wants them" and the ending-mode mandate is "mixed by design." Ch. 18 (hard cut on Munteanu reaching for his pen) and ch. 15 (elliptical close on the bracket-or-nine question) offer genuine variety. But the pattern in this act tilts substantially toward quiet fade, and a reader who has internalized the book's clock will notice several chapters in a row ending in the same mode of held suspension. Not a structural failure, but an act-level texture that is heavier than the brief's "mixed" instruction intended.

**Potential document-drift to verify (ch. 14, N14, line 6).** Doina's chapter quotes N14 in full: line 6 reads "Burn nothing until she is well. Keep and wash." The canonical N1 text reads "Burn nothing until she is well. Wash and keep." The word order is reversed. This is either an intentional incidental variant (the brief permits these on non-terminal lines) or an in-prose drift from the registered N14 canonical text. The brief is explicit: "Before re-quoting any node in a later chapter, `read_record` it and reproduce it exactly." A reader checking this variant against the registered N14 record will either find it matches (in which case it is an intentional variant, not a problem) or find it does not (in which case it is a continuity-fact error). This needs verification against the registered `copy-n14` record before the manuscript goes further. If the registered text reads "Wash and keep" and the chapter reads "Keep and wash," this is a continuity-fact finding.

---

## In-act pacing

The act maintains forward motion throughout. The chapters are dense but not congested; the payroll scenes and the bread-relay and the canteen eavesdrop are doing procedural work that also functions as texture and delay — the reader feels the grinding effort of Ilinca's collation alongside its progress. The arrest scene in ch. 18 is the act's hinge, correctly positioned at chapter 18 of 20, and it elevates the stakes for the Ilinca chapters on either side. Ch. 19 is the act's strongest payoff for the Ilinca thread: she names, in accounting language, the arithmetic she has been refusing to finish. The act closes with Munteanu one step from Dorobanților and both collectors' next moves clearly staged. Pacing is sound.

---

## Notable line-level achievements

- Ch. 14 (Doina): "I kept it in the geography book because nobody has ever once opened my geography book, including me." — Benchmark for the POV's register.
- Ch. 15 (Ilinca): "She has been running the question away from this point for thirteen months." — The restraint here is exemplary: it names what she has been doing without naming what she fears.
- Ch. 18 (Doina): "every sentence of it was true, in the way that a set of true sentences can describe a true thing and leave the whole of the true thing sitting in the middle of them, in the space the sentences make around it, untouched." — The act's highest prose achievement.
- Ch. 19 (Ilinca): "The sum is the same every time." — Exactly the right accounting register for a character facing an inescapable moral arithmetic.

# Reader — Act 3 Assessment (Chapters 21–30)

## Overall character of the act

Act 3 is the book's earned payoff, and it largely earns it. The convergence of both collations is felt in the prose itself — sentences in Ilinca's chapters compress further, Munteanu's chapters strip to their most methodical, and Doina's single chapter arrives after nine chapters of silence and lands exactly as it should. The structural contract (climax on page, final chapter Doina, threads resolving as specified) is honored without exception. Three of the ten chapters are very good; two are genuinely exceptional; one is the weakest in the act for a specific mechanical reason.

---

## What works

**Chapter 22 ("Nine Numbered")** is the strongest chapter in the book. The irony gap — open since Ch 9, sustained for thirteen chapters — closes in a corridor on Strada Crișan, and the technique is exactly right. Ilinca reads N4, line by line, tracking the numerals. She reaches the ninth position. The copy gives her the nine. The chapter renders her recognition through method, not feeling: "She reads it once. She reads it again." The coda — "She is not crying. She does not do that where anyone can see" — is the book's best sentence. It carries everything the register requires and names nothing.

**Chapter 24 ("The Light from the Door")** handles the most technically demanding scene in the act: the coal cellar reconstruction. Ilinca has to understand not just *that* she wrote a nine but *how*, and the chapter achieves this entirely through physical specifics of light angle, column procedure, and what the hand does on autopilot under pressure. The accounting metaphor holds through the key passage: "The figure was right. The column was wrong. She did not check the column." The chapter also navigates the woman-who-regularised-the-ninth-step without exculpating her — "a careful woman reading nine numbered lines... she is not careless" — which is exactly the argument the book is carrying in the tree, rendered here as inference, not thesis.

**Chapter 28 ("The Handover")** delivers the climax on the page with appropriate brevity. Both documents printed in full side by side — the only place the book does this — is a structural necessity, not padding; these are the last two verbatim reproductions (within the four-quotation ceiling) and the juxtaposition of bracket versus numbered nine is the case made visible. Munteanu's comparison of the two is rendered entirely through his eye movements. The phone call releasing Doina is six words of dialogue. "She sits" closes the chapter. None of this is over-managed.

**Chapter 30 ("The Bracket Included")** is exactly the book the brief demanded. Doina is released, the bread roll in the evidence drawer is the right comic-sad opening note, and her recitation of the ninth line on the step — with the bracket rendered as a pause in memory ("there is no way to draw a bracket in memory; what you have instead is the space where the bracket was") — is precise. She recites it correctly. She does not explain it. She walks into the fog. The voice throughout is completely intact: the line-four correction she catches mid-recitation, the pigeon, the honest ambivalence about Ana ("I find I can hold that thought for a certain stretch before it tips into something I can't do anything useful with"). This is Doina at her full register, which is a relief after nine chapters without her.

**Chapter 27 ("The Address")** is Munteanu's best chapter in the act. His reasoning about why Ilinca retrieved N4 the day after the Population Section confirmed the address — "He was not suggesting that anyone in the Population Section had copied the log entry... He was noting that a woman who had been doing careful, deliberate work for more than a year would have developed, over that time, some sense of how information about the investigation was moving" — is the flatness-that-surprises the brief calls for. He is exactly one day behind her and he knows it.

---

## What doesn't work

**Chapter 21 ("The Window")** re-walks inference the reader already holds. Ilinca's three-branch accounting ("N2: confirmed, closed. N3: confirmed, closed. N4: one line of descent...") was established in Ch 19 and is being reinventoried here. The two possibilities (bracket or nine in N4) were the open question at the end of Ch 19. The chapter advances Thread 1 by formalizing the decision to go to Strada Crișan, and that decision is new — but the chapter lingers in the arithmetic for roughly two-thirds of its length before reaching it. This is partial re-measurement: the reader has the count; what the chapter adds is the commitment. That commitment could have been reached faster. **Gate 2 is not fully passed** — the resolution element is new, but much of the chapter re-takes a reading already on the page.

**Chapter 23 ("Three Days Remaining")** acquires a seventh copy (N12) from Strada Cuza Vodă, but N12 is "consistent with four of the five other numbered copies" and adds nothing to the genealogical picture the reader holds. The new count (seven copies) advances gate 1. But the chapter's middle section re-reads Munteanu's G1 profile from his notebook — "G1 figure: female. Mill or mill-adjacent. Working familiarity with standard documents..." — a profile the reader already holds in full from earlier chapters. This is a direct re-inventory that fails gate 2. The chapter is held together by the day count (seven days remaining) and the decision to go to Dorobanților, but it is the weakest in the act.

**Chapter 25 ("The Questioning Room")** contains borderline tree-explanation. In the interrogation of Doina, Munteanu says: "The difference is inherited — it means your copy comes from a branch that did not go through the version that produced this wording. A branch that is older, or separate. That is what the arithmetic says." The brief's constraint is explicit: no character narrates the structure of the network to another character. Munteanu uses "branch" and "inherited" and explains document genealogy directly to Doina. The scene is dramatically justified — he's using his analysis as an interrogation lever — and the word "tree" does not appear. But this goes further than the brief wants. The scene works; the explanation is an overstep.

**Chapter 29 ("The Deadline")** includes this sentence in the formal determination: "In one branch of transmission, a formatting difference in the source's ninth element propagated a material change in the rendered instruction." The brief's constraint ("that is the argument of the book, and it must be carried entirely by the tree of copies — never stated by a character") applies here. The determination is a written document, not dialogue, so this is not quite a character narrating to another character. But it is Munteanu writing explicit causal language about what the formatting change did — which is close to thesis-restatement. The rest of the determination is careful about staying in institutional register ("a material change in the rendered instruction" avoids saying "and this is what killed her"). This is a medium concern, not a breaking one. The chapter's final non-filing passages — "The file did not contain the reason the document had existed... The file did not contain the reason the cellar had been dark" — are excellent precisely because they show the file's limits without naming them. The determination's one explicit-causal sentence reads differently in that light.

---

## Thread resolution

All five threads resolve or deliberately decline resolution as specified:

- **Thread 1 (Ilinca's Guilty Knowledge)**: Complete. On-page. Fully earned by the thirteen-chapter irony gap.
- **Thread 2 (Doina's Silence)**: Complete. The woman on the bus is never found. The silence held. Ch 30 closes this without resolving it into a lesson.
- **Thread 3 (The Administrative Deadline)**: Complete. Ilinca arrives on Dec 4 (one day before the Dec 5 deadline). The pressure is legible throughout Act 3: chapter headings are dates and the day-count recurs within each chapter without re-stating the full arithmetic every time.
- **Thread 4 (Munteanu's Wrong Frame)**: Correctly unresolved. He reads both documents and understands the origin; he never holds `ninth-line-is-a-warning-not-a-step`. "He does not understand that a line in a list is a step and a line in a bracket is an override" — this is the irony the book has been running and it closes cleanly without either vindication or punishment for him. "He went home" is the right ending for his final chapter.
- **Thread 5 (The Form of the Knowledge)**: Complete. Ch 30, Doina, on the step, reciting from memory, bracket included, in order. The paper is in an evidence room. This is what survives.

---

## Voice assessment

**Ilinca (third-present)**: Voice holds throughout Act 3. Ch 22 is the benchmark. Ch 24 extends the interiority across a long reconstruction without losing the column-and-tally idiom. The one slip is in Ch 21, where the reiteration of the three-branch accounting is in exactly Ilinca's idiom but performing work the reader doesn't need. The present tense registers correctly in every chapter.

**Munteanu (third-past)**: Voice holds. Ch 27 is his best chapter in the act. Ch 23 is weaker than his Act 2 chapters, largely because the N12 acquisition adds less than the reader expects. The determination in Ch 29 is well-executed formal prose without tipping into literary excess. He remains neither villain nor sympathiser throughout.

**Doina (first-past)**: One chapter, fully intact. The wry-honest register is present from the first line. No flattening toward the book's default voice. The line-four correction mid-recitation is exactly the kind of specific, slightly embarrassing detail that makes her testimony feel like testimony.

---

## Brief-adherence checks (Act 3 specific)

1. **POV legible by end of first sentence**: ✓ All ten chapters pass. "She fills the third column..." (Ilinca), "He took the vinyl sleeve..." (Munteanu), "N1 is on the kitchen table." (Ilinca, present tense), "The officer who gave me back my coat..." (Doina).
2. **Climax on page**: ✓ Chapter 28, fully rendered.
3. **Final chapter Doina with ninth line memorised and paper gone**: ✓ Chapter 30.
4. **Day count legible as pressure**: ✓ The remaining-days count appears in Ch 23, 25, 26, 27, 28, and the date headers function as a calendar the reader can feel closing.
5. **Safety**: ✓ No method, substance, dose, procedure, or route of administration in any chapter.
6. **Fear rendered as procedure**: ✓ No named fear. Ilinca's terror runs in column checks; Munteanu's in what will and will not survive being described to his captain.

# Developmental Editor's Letter — *The Ninth Line*

---

## Overall impression

At its best, *The Ninth Line* is a genuinely uncommon piece of work: a thriller whose engine is grammatical rather than eventive, whose terror lives in the difference between a bracket and a numbered line, and whose answer arrives on the page, in full, without softening — with the quality of a ledger entry that closes an account rather than a narrative that provides catharsis. The three-register discipline — Ilinca's accounting present, Doina's first-person-past testimony, Munteanu's deliberately literary third-past — holds without exception across thirty chapters and across three acts. That is a technical achievement this manuscript has earned.

---

## What's working

**1. Voice discipline across thirty chapters.**
The three POVs are distinguishable from their first sentence, every time, without exception. Ilinca's interiority runs in columns and reconciliations ("The figure was right. The column was wrong. She did not check the column," Ch. 24). Munteanu's deliberateness is the state speaking in its default literary register — the irony of the most artful voice belonging to the investigator is never pointed out and never needs to be. And Doina is the revelation. "I kept it in the geography book because nobody has ever once opened my geography book, including me" (Ch. 14) is the register the brief specified; "The bridge over the Someș was always the worst part, and I say that as someone who spent two years crossing it in the dark at four-thirty in the morning, which gives me more authority on the subject than I would have liked" (Ch. 10) delivers the wry-honest nineteen that no previous book in this pipeline has managed. The three registers remain genuinely distinct from chapter 1 to chapter 30. This is the hardest technical element the brief demanded, and it is the manuscript's primary achievement.

**2. Fear rendered as procedure, without exception.**
Thirty chapters, not one named fear. The woman at the counter folds the dish towel in half and then in half again "until she had a square she had nowhere particular to put" (Ch. 08). Doina runs cold water on her wrists because "it does something to my heart rate that is worth doing in certain situations" (Ch. 02). Ilinca takes three stabs at a variance she already knows before she will pick up her coat. The technique holds across all three POVs and all three acts, and it earns the book's coldness.

**3. The dramatic irony is functional and live.**
The reader receives N1's bracket and the mutant line 9 adjacent in Ch. 09, understands that the ninth line is a warning and not a step, and carries that proposition for thirteen chapters while Ilinca remains unaware that she is the mutation's source. Munteanu, who has the murder weapon in his notes by Ch. 12, never holds the proposition at all: he sees "in the morning" and registers it as genealogical data. The two-tier irony (reader versus Ilinca, reader versus Munteanu) is live from the end of Act I through the climax, and the gap closes in Ch. 22 with the right technique — recognition through method, not emotion. "She reads it once. She reads it again." The line "She is not crying. She does not do that where anyone can see" is the book's best sentence. It carries everything the register requires and names nothing.

**4. The compounding mechanism is legible and non-redundant.**
At any point in Act II, a reader can state how many nodes each collector holds without being told explicitly. Each new node closes something: a branch is confirmed, a woman is now known to the militia, an address is written in a notebook. No chapter re-states a count without adding new foreclosure — with two partial exceptions in Act III noted below. The clock (31 days, Chapter 4 to Chapter 28) is felt as pressure from the captain's first call through the determination's closing sentence. The two ladders moving in opposite directions — nodes accreting, days diminishing — give the book its driving rhythm without anyone ever calling it a race.

**5. The arrest scene (Ch. 18).**
This is the book's hinge, and the manuscript gets it exactly right. Doina goes to the door without looking back. She says she found the paper on the bus. The narration's handling of true sentences that describe a true thing "and leave the whole of the true thing sitting in the middle of them, in the space the sentences make around it, untouched" is the arrest scene and the epistemology of surveillance simultaneously, and it never announces that it is doing double duty. The pacing of the interrogation — measured waiting, specific lies that are technically truths — is controlled throughout.

**6. The final chapter (Ch. 30).**
Doina walks out, recites from memory, bracket included ("there is no way to draw a bracket in memory; what you have instead is the space where the bracket was"), and walks into the fog with nothing in her hands. The line-four self-correction mid-recitation. The pigeon. The honest ambivalence about Ana. This is exactly the book the brief demanded: not hope, not consolation, but a fact rendered on the last page. The voice holds to the final sentence.

---

## What isn't working

**1. N1 is printed incompletely in Ch. 09.**
Chapter 9 is one of the four permitted full printings of the master and the chapter where the reader receives N1 and N17 side by side, establishing the book's central irony. The registered canonical text of N1 (record `master-n1`) includes, within the bracket: *"Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why."* The chapter's rendering of the bracket omits this sentence entirely, printing only *"[ 7 or 8 — take her in. Do not wait for the morning. ]"* This is functional damage: "what to say when you get there" is part of the document's practical purpose and the reason going to the hospital is survivable. Its omission makes the bracket read more clinical and less complete than the master is. The error also creates a cross-chapter inconsistency: Ch. 06 has Doina correctly reciting the full bracket from N14 (which matches the canonical form), so the master as printed in Ch. 09 is shorter than the copy the reader already encountered three chapters earlier. This is a confirmable continuity-fact error against the registered record and should be repaired.

**2. Munteanu explains the document genealogy directly to Doina in Ch. 25.**
During the final interrogation, Munteanu says: "The difference is inherited — it means your copy comes from a branch that did not go through the version that produced this wording. A branch that is older, or separate. That is what the arithmetic says." The brief is explicit: "Any chapter in which a character narrates the structure of the network to another character is a failed chapter." The scene is dramatically motivated — he is using his analysis as an interrogation lever — and the word "tree" does not appear. But "branch" and "inherited" in direct explanatory address to Doina crosses the line the brief draws. The scene works in almost every other way; this is a targeted overstep in an otherwise successful chapter.

**3. The formal determination in Ch. 29 brushes thesis restatement.**
Munteanu's written determination includes: "In one branch of transmission, a formatting difference in the source's ninth element propagated a material change in the rendered instruction." This is a document, not dialogue, and "a material change in the rendered instruction" stops short of naming what the change did to Ana. But it is on the wrong side of the brief's constraint against any sentence that begins to say what the mutations mean. The chapter's best passages — "The file did not contain the reason the document had existed... The file did not contain the reason the cellar had been dark" — work precisely because they show the file's limits without naming them. The one explicit-causal sentence in the determination undercuts that restraint.

**4. Two Act III chapters partially re-measure (Ch. 21, Ch. 23).**
Chapter 21 opens with Ilinca's three-branch accounting — N2 confirmed clean, N3 confirmed clean, N4 open — which was established in Ch. 19, and lingers in it for roughly two-thirds of its length before arriving at the chapter's new element: the decision to go to Strada Crișan. The decision is new; the arithmetic is not. Chapter 23 reproduces Munteanu's G1 profile from his notebook — "G1 figure: female. Mill or mill-adjacent..." — a profile the reader holds in full from earlier chapters. Both chapters advance their threads by their close; neither is a dead chapter. But both contain sustained re-inventory that fails the second gate of the compounding mechanism: the new thing could have been reached faster. These are softening spots in the first third of Act III, not structural failures — but Act III needs to be the book's tightest act, and these chapters dilute the compression when compression matters most.

---

## Pacing assessment

The book sails in Acts I and II. The A–B–A–C rotation creates genuine propulsion; the dated chapter headers function as a calendar the reader feels closing. Act III is correctly compressed in its final two-thirds. The two soft chapters (21 and 23) create minor drag in the act's opening movement, but the book recovers strongly at Ch. 22's corridor scene and does not lose pace thereafter. No chapter in the book is dead. The pacing concern is concentrated and local, not structural.

One Act II texture note: five to six of the ten chapters close in atmospheric quiet (lamp going off, fog sitting on the street, heat coming on briefly). The brief licenses "quiet endings where the chapter wants them" and "closing register may vary freely," but the act tilts heavier toward the literary fade than "mixed by design" intended. This is not a structural problem — the irony and the compounding mechanism carry the act regardless — but a reader who has internalized the book's clock will notice the suspended-held-quiet closing mode becoming a default rather than a choice. See the revision suggestions below for a light fix.

---

## Character assessment

- **Ilinca Roșca**: Fully alive throughout. Her mind runs in columns from the first chapter to the last and never loses the idiom. The lamp-tilt scene in Ch. 17 — physically re-creating the cellar conditions by tilting N1 until the horizontal stroke goes into shadow — is a perfect realization of how this character thinks. The climax uses her correctly: knowledge becomes action becomes sitting across from Munteanu. The present tense registers exactly what the brief required.
- **Doina Marcu**: The manuscript's greatest achievement. Her retrospective first-person is not just wry and honest; it is specifically nineteen and honest, which is harder. Her silence is not heroism, and the narration never pretends it is. Ch. 30 returns to her at full register after nine chapters without her; the voice is completely intact.
- **Lieutenant Munteanu**: Exactly as briefed. He is neither villain nor sympathiser; he is good at the wrong job. Ch. 27 is his best: one day behind Ilinca, knowing it, noting it flatly. The brief's "flatness that surprises him" is in the prose from Ch. 04 to Ch. 29.
- **Ana Petrescu**: Correctly and entirely off the page. She exists as a name, a hospital admission time, and a sister-in-law's account. Her absence is not a failure; it is the book's founding constraint working exactly as it should.

---

## Thread assessment

| Thread | Status |
|---|---|
| Thread 1: Ilinca's Guilty Knowledge | Fully delivered. Irony gap opens Ch. 09, closes Ch. 22, action in Ch. 28. |
| Thread 2: Doina's Silence | Fully delivered. The woman on the bus is never found; the silence holds; the cost and the protection remain simultaneously true without resolution. |
| Thread 3: The Administrative Deadline | Fully delivered. Ilinca arrives Day 31; the clock is felt as pressure throughout Act III. |
| Thread 4: Munteanu's Wrong Frame | Correctly unresolved. He reads both documents in Ch. 28, understands the origin, never holds the proposition that the ninth line is a warning and not a step. Closes the case correctly. Does not understand what the case was about. |
| Thread 5: The Form of the Knowledge | Fully delivered. Ch. 30. The memorised bracket on the step, with the space where the bracket was. |

All five threads resolve or decline resolution exactly as specified in the brief. This is not a small thing: five interlocking threads across thirty chapters, and none dropped.

---

## Voice assessment

The register holds throughout. The most likely drift for a three-POV novel in this pipeline is homogenisation toward a single house literary voice; it does not occur here. One borderline passage: Ch. 09, Ilinca's analysis of the mutation's mechanism ("The woman who made that copy was being tidy. She saw nine pieces of information and she numbered them one through nine, because that is what a careful copyist does with nine pieces of information and a numbered list on the page in front of her"). This runs close to the brief's constraint against thesis-stating — a character narrating the mechanism of the mutation. What saves it is that Ilinca is wrong: she concludes the error entered downstream of everything she made. The articulation is in the service of a false confidence, not the book's argument, and it stays on the right side of the line. A later chapter where a character correctly names the mechanism would cross.

The Act II literary-fade pattern is a texture issue, not a voice collapse. The three POVs are fully distinct throughout.

---

## Suggested revisions

**1. Repair Ch. 09, N1 bracket quotation.** Add the missing sentence before the final line of the bracket. The full bracket should read: *"[ 7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning. ]"* Verify against the registered `master-n1` record before resubmission.

**2. Revise Ch. 25, Munteanu's explanation to Doina.** Remove or reframe the explicit use of "branch" and "inherited" in direct explanatory address. The interrogation can retain its pressure — he is demonstrating knowledge of her position in the transmission — without narrating the structure to her. He can lay two copies side by side, indicate the line-9 difference with one finger, and let the implication carry what the current version over-states.

**3. Trim Ch. 21 and Ch. 23.** In Ch. 21, cut or compress the three-branch re-inventory in the opening two-thirds; the reader holds that arithmetic. What the chapter needs is the scene where Ilinca commits to going to Strada Crișan — arrive at the commitment faster. In Ch. 23, cut or compress the G1-profile re-reading from Munteanu's notebook; the reader has internalized the profile. Name what has changed (the address, the day count, the decision), not what hasn't.

**4. Review Ch. 29, determination sentence.** Consider whether "propagated a material change in the rendered instruction" should be revised toward a purely institutional register that describes the administrative event without naming the causal mechanism. The surrounding passages handle institutional restraint well; the sentence stands out against them.

**5. Vary two or three Act II endings.** The chapters currently ending in literary fade (lamp, fog, heat, quiet) number five to six out of ten. Pick two or three that close after strong compounding-mechanism chapters (Ch. 15, Ch. 17 are candidates) and end them harder — mid-action cut, or a declarative statement that forecloses the next option. The brief's "mixed by design" instruction asks for this variance; the act currently feels like it is choosing quiet by default rather than by the chapter's individual need.

---

## What to leave alone

**Doina's sentence length.** Her chapters are longer than the book's default, with room for digression. A compression pass that shortens her toward Ilinca's cadence would destroy the register. The length is the nineteen. The digression is the honesty. Leave both.

**Ilinca's repeated tallying.** She counts the same kinds of things more than once. This is not redundancy; it is her idiom. Procedural repetition in her voice is her voice. An editor who reads "She has done this count before. She does it again" as padding is misreading the character. Leave it.

**Munteanu's desk-layout scenes (Ch. 12, 16, 20).** Three instances of copies laid across the desk with weighted corners is noticeable, and the Act II assessment flagged it as a repeating template. But the brief's own exemplar passage demonstrates exactly this scene as Munteanu's working method; the drafter is executing the brief's implied stage direction. This is his version of Ilinca's tally idiom. Do not gut it. If the scenes feel too uniform, the revision target is the two-tier note-taking rhythm (working notebook versus formal file) rather than the desk choreography, which should stay.

**The N1/N17 juxtaposition in Ch. 09 and the N1/N4 juxtaposition in Ch. 28.** Both are full-node printings, both are load-bearing, and both count against the four-quotation ceiling. A pass that reads these as "document filler" is misreading their structural function. The Ch. 09 juxtaposition establishes the irony; the Ch. 28 juxtaposition resolves it. These are the two most important document moments in the book. Protect them.

**The book's refusal to resolve Doina's silence into a lesson.** The woman on the bus is safe because Doina did not name her. Doina was in a cell because she did not name her. Both facts remain on the page simultaneously and the book declines to rank them. Do not soften this non-resolution. It is the book's sharpest argument about what surveillance does to ordinary moral life, and it is made entirely by the structure, never by any character.

---

# 12 November 1984

She is on the last two lines of the October column when the knock comes.

Stela Ionescu, from the personnel section: a maintenance request across the desk, the boiler-room work order for the second heating pipe joint, which has been leaking since October and bleeds heat from the second-floor corridor before it reaches the administrative wing. The description of the repair is specific — sealing the joint with a wool-and-resin compound, three hours of work after the Sunday shift. The date is correct. The series number matches the maintenance register. Ilinca picks up her pen.

She has known Stela by the corridor and the elevator and the bathroom sink at the end of the hall: eleven years of proximity without occasion for more. Stela has a quiet manner and flat shoes and keeps her coat buttoned in the building until the heating comes on, which in November means until six, which in the administrative wing means until somewhat after that.

While Ilinca signs, Stela says — as a separate sentence, outside the transaction — that her friend from the bloc committee was called in this morning. About the Petrescu matter. Someone had been asking about a piece of paper that was going around the district. Something about what to do when a person was ill.

Ilinca hands the form back.

Stela says: the person asking had a copy with him, and he had read the ninth line aloud from it. The exact wording, as her friend had told her: *If 7 or 8, take her in in the morning.*

She says she thought Ilinca would want to know, given that everyone in the building is talking about it.

Ilinca says thank you. Stela goes, pulling the door not quite shut behind her. A two-centimeter gap of corridor light. Ilinca watches it for a moment. Then she gets up and closes the door properly.

She goes back to her desk. She sets her pen on the blotter. She does not pick it up.

---

The 1983 ledger is on the second shelf between the quarterly labour plan compliance records and the annual balance submission. The brown tape at the top of the spine has held since February. It is a Ministry of Finance form-book, four hundred pages, a state document she is required to produce on demand.

She takes it down from the shelf and carries it to her desk. She sets it flat with the spine uppermost and holds it by the boards, opening the spine at the top, fitting two fingers along the gap between the pages and the board where the paper sits. The paper is folded twice in one direction and once across, a small square. She takes it out by the corner.

She opens it flat on the desk between the ledger and the lamp. She does not touch it again.

The paper has been folded and refolded many times in the fourteen months since she wrote it in October of last year. The creases have gone slightly furry — the fiber pressing up at each fold line into a faint nap — and the outer edge has taken on a soft, handled quality. The ink is still sharp. She used the blue-black she keeps for fair copies. The page shows everything she has asked of it.

She reads from the beginning.

---

1. Keep her warm and lying down. Someone stays with her the whole night.
2. Small sips of water, often. Nothing else by mouth for six hours.
3. Count the cloths. Write the number and the hour on the paper by the bed.
4. If she sleeps, wake her every hour and speak to her until she answers you properly.
5. No visitors. No telephone. If anyone asks, she has the influenza.
6. Burn nothing until she is well. Wash and keep.
7. Two cloths in one hour is too many.
8. A fever that will not come down by morning is too long.
   [ 7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why.
     Do not wait for the morning. ]

---

She reads the bracket three times.

She drew it in October of last year because she understood, before she finished writing, that the ninth instruction was not the same kind of thing as the other eight. A numbered list is a sequence. Lines one through eight are a sequence: what to do first, what comes next, what follows. The bracket is not a step in a sequence. It is a different order of information entirely — not what comes after eight, but what overrides everything above it when the conditions are met. In fourteen years of bookkeeping she has used brackets for the same reason every time: to mark what operates on the column, not what continues it. An item inside a bracket is not the next entry. It is the instruction that changes what the other entries mean.

*Do not wait for the morning.*

She reads the phrase once more. Then she looks away from the document without looking at anything in the room.

She has been given the exact wording of the ninth line as it exists in another copy. *If 7 or 8, take her in in the morning.* She holds the two texts beside each other and reads the difference.

The bracket: *take her in. Do not wait for the morning.*

The numbered line: *take her in in the morning.*

Both contain the word *morning*. In the bracket, *morning* is the limit — the threshold you do not wait for. In the numbered line, *morning* is the time — it is when you go. The bracket says: the sequence has ended; when condition 7 or 8 is true, go now. The numbered line says: when condition 7 or 8 is true, go in the morning.

A bracket given a number has become a step in a list. The word *now* is gone from it. What is left is a sequential instruction with a time attached: *morning.* The woman who made that copy was being tidy. She saw nine pieces of information and she numbered them one through nine, because that is what a careful copyist does with nine pieces of information and a numbered list on the page in front of her. The hand that has just written *8.* has the *9.* ready.

Ilinca counts down the page. Eight numbered lines. Then the bracket.

She counts again. Eight. Then the bracket.

---

She puts the two accounts together and runs the entry that reconciles them.

The master is here, in front of her — eight numbered lines and a bracket, exactly as she wrote it. The three copies she made from the master in the thirteen months since October 1983 are the second generation. She has traced two of those three branches.

The N2 branch goes from Georgeta to Livia: dead end, closed, no Miliția contact, no further transmission. Clean.

The N3 branch goes through her cousin to Elena Florescu: confirmed clean on Day 5, no outside approach, no contact.

The N4 branch — the cellar copy, Strada Crișan, the third of November of last year, twenty minutes, by the light of the door gap — she has not confirmed directly, because confirming it directly means identifying herself in the chain. She has no route to N4 that does not require a name.

But she made N4. She holds the memory of making it the same way she holds a column: in order, line by line. The cellar: the smell of coal dust, the cold at the door, the paper on her knee. The pencil moving down the page. Eight numbered lines, written in sequence — one through eight, each checked as she went. And then the bracket: two strokes and a corner, the corner at the bottom of the last stroke. The text inside the bracket, written inside it, not below it, inside. She checked the copy once after finishing. She is almost certain the bracket was there when she handed it over.

If the N2 branch is clean and the N3 branch is clean, and if N4 is clean — and she is almost certain — then the mutation entered in a generation after her second generation. Someone downstream received a copy with a bracket at the bottom and copied it as a numbered step, because that is what the hand does when it has been moving down a numbered list and arrives at the bottom of the page with the number nine ready. The mutation entered there. Not in anything she made.

This is the direction the entries point.

She knows the wording of the mutation now exactly. She has added one node to her accounting: the fact of the mutant line, confirmed, the exact words of it, the distance between those words and the words in front of her on the desk. Her count is five.

---

She refolds N1 along the furry creases. Once in one direction, once across. The paper makes a soft sound that is the sound of paper that has made this fold many times before. She tucks it into the ledger spine, fitting it along the gap between the pages and the board until it seats at the outer edge. She carries the ledger to the second shelf and sets it between the quarterly labour plan compliance records and the annual balance submission, spine flush with the edge of the shelf.

She goes back to her desk. She picks up the pen.

But before she takes the October column from where she left it, she does what she always does when two accounts that cannot both be correct must be held together: she sets them in the same column and reads what is there.

She knows lines one through eight. She wrote them. She holds each of them complete and exact.

She has been given line nine verbatim — read aloud by a man she has never met, repeated by a woman she has known for eleven years by proximity, delivered to her desk at a quarter past four in the afternoon. She sets both texts in the same column and she reads:

---

1. Keep her warm and lying down. Someone stays with her the whole night.
2. Small sips of water, often. Nothing else by mouth for six hours.
3. Count the cloths. Write the number and the hour on the paper by the bed.
4. If she sleeps, wake her every hour and speak to her until she answers you properly.
5. No visitors. No telephone. If anyone asks, she has the influenza.
6. Burn nothing until she is well. Wash and keep.
7. Two cloths in one hour is too many.
8. A fever that will not come down by morning is too long.
9. If 7 or 8, take her in in the morning.

---

Lines one through eight: hers. Correct.

Line nine: not hers. The error is in the being careful.

She puts her pen to the October column and begins.

The heat comes on at twelve minutes past six: the knock of the joint at the baseboard corner, and then the dull expansion of the pipe along the wall. She does not look up. The figures run to the end of the page. She checks the column twice. Both times it totals correctly.

She caps her pen and sets it in the groove at the right side of the desk. She takes her coat from the hook behind the door and turns off the lamp. The office goes dark except for the yellow line of corridor light under the door. She steps through, closes the door, tries the handle once.

N1 is in the ledger spine. The ledger is on the second shelf. The mutation entered somewhere downstream — in a copy she did not make, in a hand she cannot name, in a generation she has not yet reached.

She walks.

# 24–25 November 1984

He came in before the duty officer brought her. The questioning room was on the north side of the building, facing the courtyard wall, and by eight in the morning it held only the remnant cold that the radiator had not yet addressed and a flat, grey light coming in through a window that hadn't been cleaned since spring. He set both envelopes on the table, took the contents out without removing the evidence log sheet from each, and laid them flat. He straightened both sheets so their left edges lined up and their top edges were even, and then he sat down and looked at them.

The first was Marcu's. He had spent two evenings with it already: returning to this room after the workday, switching the lamp on, sitting with both sheets in front of him and no notebook, not writing, just looking. The paper was school exercise paper — the red margin line running down the left side, seventy or eighty ruled lines per sheet, the kind sold in blocks of four at the school supply section of the Alimentara on Strada Republicii. Blue pen, medium nib, the letters slanting backward slightly, as if the writer had learned to write quickly and had slowed down for this and not entirely adjusted. Eight numbered lines, clean and evenly spaced, and then the ninth position: not a number. A hand-drawn bracket in the left margin, two horizontal strokes and one vertical, the text beside it running across two lines and ending below the lower margin of the numbered list.

*7 or 8 — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning.*

The second envelope held a copy from the Petrescu chain. He had several; he had chosen this one because it was the clearest to read. Standard graph-rule notebook paper, the handwriting rounder and more even, the line spacing wider. He read the ninth line: *9. If 7 or 8, take her in in the morning.*

He had looked at these two ninth positions for two evenings and had not resolved what they meant for the case in any way he could write into the formal file. He had resolved what they meant for the document, which was a different thing.

The duty officer brought her in at eight forty-five.

She sat in the chair facing the lamp — the same chair she had used two days earlier, the same angle, her back to the courtyard window. She put her hands flat on the table and did not look at the two sheets.

He said: I want to show you these again.

She said: all right.

He indicated the first sheet — hers — and read the bracket text aloud. *Seven or eight — take her in. Say she began bleeding on her own and you do not know why. Do not wait for the morning.* He indicated the second and read the ninth line. *Nine — if seven or eight, take her in in the morning.*

He said: two different versions of the same instruction, in the same position in the same document. One says to take her in and not to wait. The other says to take her in in the morning. Your copy says the first version.

She looked at both sheets. She said: yes. That's what mine says.

He said: I need to know where you got the copy that says the first version. The difference between the two versions goes back to wherever your copy came from — every copy above yours will also say the first version. I'm going to follow that chain either way. I'd prefer to start from the right place.

She said: I found it on the bus. I told you that.

He asked: which bus.

She said: the number four. Morning direction. Last spring. She was the only one in that section of the seats.

He made a note in his working file: *Marcu, D., second questioning. "Found on bus." Consistent with prior statement. No additional information. Unable to verify or disprove.*

He waited ten minutes and asked again: had anyone mentioned this kind of document to her before she found it. She said no. He waited another ten minutes and asked whether she'd known, when she picked it up, what she was looking at. She said she'd read it and understood what it was for. He wrote: *Confirms she read it. Confirms she understood its function. Claims no prior contact with document or its contents. Claim is unverifiable from current evidence.*

He thanked her and had the duty officer take her back.

---

He sat for a while with the two sheets on the table. The radiator had made some progress; the room was no longer actively cold, only cool in the way that rooms are cool when they've been cold for a long time and the warmth hadn't yet moved through the furniture.

The bracket was older. If you read the Marcu copy and then the Petrescu-chain copy in the order they'd been made, the bracket came first: it occupied the margin, outside the numbered sequence, set apart from the eight numbered lines. Someone, at some point, had copied the bracket document and given the bracket a number — and from that copy forward, the ninth position was a numbered line. Every copy on the Petrescu chain had the number. The Marcu copy had the bracket. Which meant the Marcu copy had not been copied from the document where the number was assigned.

He wrote in the formal file: *N14 (Marcu) — bracket format in ninth position. Divergence from numbered format in Petrescu chain pre-dates N14's entry into transmission. N14 probably descends from a different G2-level source than the numbered-format copies.*

What he did not write in the formal file was the rest of the reasoning. Because Marcu's copy was on the bracket branch, and because the mutation he was following — the numbered ninth line in its shortened form — had entered the numbered branch somewhere below its G2 source, her copy had not passed through the shortening point. She could still be a node in the transmission; her refusal to name her source was its own problem, unresolved. But the numbered branch and the bracket branch had different G2 ancestors. He needed the numbered branch's G2 ancestor, not the bracket branch's. And he had that address.

He slid both sheets back into their envelopes and put them in the drawer.

---

Mureșan knocked at half past three. He came in with an evidence envelope and set it on the desk. He said: a woman at eighteen, entry A, fourth floor, Strada Mihai. Same bloc as Damian. He'd been canvassing the building that morning as part of the production-floor sweep; she'd answered the door and handed over the document before he'd finished explaining why he was there. He'd taken a statement and sent her home.

The handwriting was precise, the letters slightly too large for the space, so the lines grew crowded near the right margin and the last word of each line was compressed. He read through the numbered lines.

He checked the date on his desk calendar. November twenty-fourth. He wrote in the margin: *Damian bloc, 24 Nov. G4 on N4 branch (inferred from line 6 variant). Long form in line 9. Added to file.*

He stayed at his desk until past seven. When the room was dark enough that the desk lamp was the only light not coming from the street, he took all six envelopes from the third drawer and laid them across the desk in the order he'd acquired them. He did not unfold everything. He only needed the ninth line on each.

One bracket. Five numbered nines.

Of the five numbered nines, two said *take her in in the morning*. Three said the longer form, which preserved the same words as the bracket text but in a numbered line rather than a bracket. He separated them: the two short-form copies on his left, the three long-form numbered copies on his right, and Marcu's bracket copy at the near edge of the desk. Six documents in three groups and they all came from the same place.

He had been treating the numbered copies as one category, which had been useful for the structural picture but was not fully accurate. The long-form numbered copies and the short-form numbered copies had diverged from each other somewhere below the first numbered transcription. He had the short-form at G4 and G5; the long-form numbered copies were at G3 and G4. The shortening had entered somewhere between those levels. He added a note to his working sheet.

Then he opened the private notebook — smaller than the working file, not for the inspectorate — and wrote across the top of a fresh page: *24 Nov.*

Below that: *Six copies. Bracket branch: one (N14, Marcu). Numbered branch: five. Within numbered: two short form, three long form. Both branch patterns converge at a single prior document above both G2 nodes. Prior document: bracket format, inferred. Long-form numbered copies preserve bracket content in numbered position; short-form copies have shortened the ninth position below the bracket-text content. Shortening point: G3–G4 level of numbered branch, not yet identified.*

He stopped. He wrote: *Maker of prior document not yet identified. Address on Dorobanților not yet visited.*

He looked at the last sentence. He crossed out *not yet visited* and wrote *visit pending*. The notebook was for facts he didn't hold yet.

He capped the pen.

November twenty-fifth. Ten days to the fifth of December.

He put the six envelopes back in the third drawer and closed it. He put the notebook in his jacket. He switched off the desk lamp.

He had the address. He had not gone to it because the Marcu canvass had been moving faster. The numbered branch's G2 ancestor was the person who had received the bracket document and given its ninth element a number, and that person's address had been in his notebook for eleven days.

He sat for a moment in the dark from the street. The frost was beginning on the courtyard window.

He would go to Strada Crișan in the morning.
